name: Minar-e-Pakistan
assumptions: Total 70 m and tower 62 m above the base are the dossier values; the star top is therefore 8 m up, though photos suggest the visible plinth may be lower.
Intermediate tier heights (1.8, 3.4, 5.0, 6.4, 7.7 m) are estimates that climb to the sourced 8 m.
Plan radii, the teardrop outline, bridges and rostrum position were measured on one satellite image and may carry about 1 m of error.
Tier order of the four sourced stones is taken as outermost uncut to innermost marble; colours are photo estimates.
Petal height is 9.9 m as measured in the telephoto photo; sources say 9 m.
Ten petals and ten ribs: counted on the aerial image; rib phase is set so one arch is centred on the plaza axis.
Tower radii and floor bands were read from one telephoto photo and ignore perspective.
Core treated as a dark glazed cylinder with a helical stair; its true construction was not seen.
Lantern has six arches, inferred from two visible arch spacings; dome flute count is an estimate.
Red pool assigned to the arc facing the teardrop and green to the far arc, from one oblique aerial; the actual division is unconfirmed.
Rostrum drawn as a low tiled wedge at the teardrop point; its height and pattern are unknown.
Door on the axis and plaques on the drum faces: the positions of the ten plaques are not published.
Night glow is a neutral white wash; the real LED colours vary.
